expect.note: The value /version serves is one the build DERIVED for itself, and the mechanism is graded, not the route (the route is `version-never-guesses-a-build-sha`'s job and its 13 probes are untouched). Four conjuncts: .dockerignore admits `.git` into the build context; the Dockerfile declares no `ARG ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` (the 2026-08-28 live read proved the platform never fills it, so the only feeder left was a hand-typed dashboard build-arg value that every later build would re-bake -- ADR-033 Decision 2's rejected path at build time, PR #65 R3); the derivation RUN line, extracted by regex and EXECUTED with substituted paths, writes this checkout's HEAD when pointed at the repo root and exits 0 leaving an EMPTY file when pointed at a git-less directory -- empty being exactly what /version answers `unavailable` for; and `.git` never reaches the final image -- the derivation lives in an earlier stage on the same base tag and the final stage COPYs exactly one file back out of it. Both COPY conjuncts are graded on the SOURCE, not the destination: the derive stage must copy the whole context (`.`) or `.git` itself, and no final-stage COPY may take `.` or anything naming `.git` (PR #67 R1/R2). Each is exercised by a mutation the check runs itself, so neither is a claim about a line nobody breaks.

provenance:
M44-P1 remedy phase, written before the Dockerfile changed. ADR-033 deliberately left one fact unverified -- whether Zeabur passes its Git-group variables to a Dockerfile build -- and designed the route to fail to the honest null if not. The first deploy after PR #65's merge (6089850) settled it, on 2026-08-28: `curl https://whaleforce-browser-agent.zeabur.app/version` answered {"sha":null,"source":"unavailable"} while /healthz was ok, so the new build IS running and the ARG is never filled. ADR-033 Consequences pre-recorded exactly this outcome and its sole remedy: a sha the build derives for itself. ADR-034 is the ruling; this case is its mechanism guard.

RED, watched, against the pre-remedy tree (the merged PR #65 Dockerfile and .dockerignore, unmodified): 4 of the check's conjunct keys fired at once -- dockerignore_excludes_git ['.git'], build_arg_still_declared ['ARG ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA=""'], single_stage ('1 FROM line(s)'), derive_command_missing. The two executed probes could not fire on that tree (no derive command to extract), which is why the shape conjuncts exist separately: a red that only said 'command missing' would go green on any RUN line shaped right, executed or not.

The fail-to-empty probe was then mutation-tested on a scratch copy of the FIXED Dockerfile, because an executed probe never seen red proves nothing (rule 2): with the `|| : > /BUILD_SHA` fallback deleted from the derive RUN line, the extraction still matches (the fallback group is optional in the regex ON PURPOSE, so a fallback-less variant is extracted and executed rather than reported as a shape miss) and `gitless-context-empty-file` went red with exit 128 -- `git rev-parse` failing in a directory with no repository and nothing catching it, the exact build behaviour that would break a deploy whose context lacks `.git` instead of publishing the honest `unavailable`. A second mutation, deriving from a directory the stage never COPYs into (`-C /nowhere`), was predicted to redden the executed head probe and instead went red one conjunct earlier, on `derive_stage_never_copies_the_context` -- recorded as it happened, not as predicted: the shape conjunct fires first because an un-COPY'd context is visible statically, and what that red demonstrates is THAT conjunct's non-vacuity. The `derives-this-checkouts-head` probe itself has no reachable in-shape Dockerfile mutation today (the extraction regex admits essentially one command); what it executes against every run is the extraction-and-substitution machinery, and its declared job is to catch a future widening of that regex admitting a command that does not produce HEAD -- the triage note carries this as a ceiling.

Worktree caveat, recorded because this repo works in them: the derivation copies the CONTEXT's `.git`, and in a git worktree that is a pointer file into a repository the copy does not include, so a docker build FROM A WORKTREE would produce the honest empty file. The executed probes are immune -- they point the extracted command at the live checkout, where git follows the pointer -- which is also why `derives-this-checkouts-head` holds in the CI checkout and in this worktree alike.

PR #67 round 1 found both COPY conjuncts vacuous in the direction they are named for, and both are now graded through mutations the check executes against a scratch Dockerfile rather than through prose. R1: the derive stage's COPY was matched on its DESTINATION, so `COPY . /ctx` -> `COPY src /ctx` -- a subtree that cannot contain `.git` -- returned {'passed': True, 'wrong': {}} while the real build would derive nothing and /version would be `unavailable` forever. R2: `.dockerignore` used to filter `.git` out of every stage, so a whole-context COPY into the final image was harmless; this change is what makes it reachable, and `COPY src/ /app/src/` -> `COPY . /app/` shipped the entire git history into a publicly deployed image past a substring scan for `.git` that such a line never contains -- also {'passed': True, 'wrong': {}}. Both mutations were re-run here before the guards were written (green, reproducing the reviewer), then the two mutation rows were added and WATCHED RED against the round-1 guards -- {'mutation_derive-stage-copies-a-subtree_not_caught': ..., 'mutation_final-stage-copies-the-context_not_caught': ...} -- and only then were the guards fixed. They now report {'derive_stage_never_copies_the_context': {'context': '/ctx', 'copies': 'src', ...}} and {'final_stage_copies_git': ['COPY . /app/']}. Each mutation asserts its own substitution happened, so a rename that made the pattern absent is a loud `mutation_..._is_vacuous` rather than a row quietly passing on an unmutated copy.

triage.note:
Pure code plus two subprocess runs of the Dockerfile's own derive command; no browser, no network, no spend -- what `invariant` admits. `invariant`-only for ADR-033 Decision 4's reason unchanged: the `fast` band has no room and this case does not need the app at all.

Declared ceilings, in the sibling case's spirit. (1) The two textual conjuncts are scans: a new spelling of the `.git` exclusion (`.git*`, a glob, an exclusion in a nested ignore file) or of the ARG (a renamed build argument fed to the same file) is invisible; the backstop is the post-merge live read M44-P1's block requires, where a stripped or re-excluded `.git` reads `unavailable`. (2) The executed probes run the extracted command under `sh` on THIS machine -- no Docker exists here (declared in ADR-034 as in ADR-033), so what is proven is the command's behaviour, not the image's: a base image lacking `git` would fall to the `|| :` branch and publish `unavailable`, which the design accepts and the probes cannot distinguish from a platform that strips `.git`. (3) The regex admits one command shape; a semantically equivalent derive line spelled differently (a heredoc, a script COPY'd in) is `derive_command_missing` -- red, loudly, so the failure mode is a false alarm demanding the regex widen, never a silent pass. The flip side, declared: because the shape is that tight, `derives-this-checkouts-head` currently has no reachable in-shape mutation to redden it -- it exercises the extraction/substitution machinery on every run and earns its keep the day the regex is widened. (4) The stage checks are line-anchored regexes over the Dockerfile text: a `COPY` split across a line continuation is invisible. (5) The executed probes need a resolvable HEAD, so a `container:` CI job, a `git archive` tarball or an installed copy reddens a suite gated at 100% with a correct Dockerfile -- the same ceiling `version-never-guesses-a-build-sha` declares, and the same debt: `M44-P1-D2` names both functions (PR #67 R5). (6) The two COPY mutations are the two shapes review found; a third way of copying the wrong thing (a `.dockerignore` re-inclusion, a build-arg-driven path) is not among them, which is the usual bound on an exercise set. Same restore discipline as the sibling: nothing global is mutated -- the check writes only under tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and touches no module attribute, no environment variable.
